ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: After ignoring the curved arrows in the figure, an aryl ester-like structure can be seen: below is a benzene ring, connected by a single bond to an oxygen atom; this oxygen is then connected to an acyl carbon. On the right side of the acyl carbon is an unspecified R group, and upward it forms a double bond with oxygen; this carbonyl oxygen is marked with a positive charge and coordinates with the AlCl3 fragment at the upper left, with aluminum marked with a negative charge. Reasoning: The unspecified R group is represented by the wildcard atom *, so the acyl carbon is written as *C. The singly connected phenoxy substituent is written as (Oc1ccccc1). The double bond between the acyl carbon and the positively charged oxygen is written as =[O+]. This oxygen is connected to the negatively charged trichloroaluminum fragment, written as [Al-](Cl)(Cl)Cl. Combining gives the SMILES: *C(Oc1ccccc1)=[O+][Al-](Cl)(Cl)Cl.

method.method_draft: First describe the drawn molecule ignoring arrows: it is an aryl ester/acyl-oxygen complex with R-C(=O+-AlCl3)-O-Ph. Encode the acyl carbon as `*C(...)` because the R group is unspecified. Put the single-bonded phenoxy substituent in parentheses as `(Oc1ccccc1)`. Encode the double bond from the acyl carbon to positively charged oxygen as `=[O+]`, then attach the aluminum trichloride fragment as `[Al-](Cl)(Cl)Cl`. Combining these components gives `*C(Oc1ccccc1)=[O+][Al-](Cl)(Cl)Cl`.
